hook.text: The weighted sum can be any number: minus twelve, zero, three point seven. But for a class, we want a probability.

act.text: That is the job of the activation function. It takes the sum, and turns it into the unit's output.

sig.text: For two classes, we use the sigmoid. It squeezes any number into the range zero to one.

sig2.text: A big positive sum gives almost one. A big negative sum gives almost zero. And a sum of exactly zero gives zero point five.

sig3.text: So one sigmoid output is read as the probability of class one. Choose class one when it is above zero point five: that is the same as the sum being above zero.

other.text: The slides list other common ones. tanh gives values from minus one to one. ReLU keeps a positive sum, and turns a negative one into zero. For regression, the output simply stays linear.

multi.text: With more than two classes, the network has one output per class, and we use softmax.

sm1.text: Say the scores are two, one and zero. Raise e to each: about seven point three nine, two point seven two, and one.

sm2.text: Divide each by the total, eleven point one one. You get zero point six seven, zero point two four, and zero point zero nine.

sm3.text: They add up to one, and the network chooses class one, the largest. Because they share one total, the classes compete: raise one score, and the others fall.

why.text: But activations do something bigger. Look at XOR. It is one when exactly one input is one.

xor1.text: The two ones sit on one diagonal, the two zeros on the other. No single straight line can separate them.

xor2.text: So we add a hidden layer. One hidden unit draws one line, the other draws a second, and the output unit combines them.

lin.text: This works only because each hidden unit applies its activation. Without it, the network is just sums of sums, and it collapses back into one line.

when.text: And when are they used? Not before training. They are part of the network. Every forward pass applies them, in training and in prediction, and backpropagation uses their slope.

ex1.text: The activation turns the sum into the output.

ex3.text: Softmax: one output per class, summing to one.

ex4.text: Without activations, the layers collapse into one line.

ex5.text: They are used in training and in prediction.
